Card Tactics Rules

A quick reference for how PaperGames plays this card-driven race across the board.

The basic idea

The setup
The board has 7 rows and 6 columns. Black's six stones fill the bottom row, White's six stones the top row. Black starts.
Move cards
There are twelve move cards; at the start they are shuffled and each side gets six. Three of them lie open in front of their side (both players can see them), the other three face down in that side's own pile. Each card shows its moves as arrows: ↑↑ means two squares forward, ↑← one forward and one to the left, ↗ one square diagonally. Forward always means towards the other side.
Making a move
Pick one of your own three open cards, then one of your stones, then a square the card allows. You may move onto an empty square or onto an enemy stone, which is captured. Your own stones block. You never use a card of the other side.
The card pile
The top card of your own face-down pile takes the place of the card you used, and the used card goes back into your pile at a hidden place. So you never know which of your cards comes next, and your cards never go to the other side.
Opening move
The starter's first move goes one row at most, and their second move may not go two rows straight ahead. This evens out the advantage of starting.
No move possible
If you cannot move, you pass, and your first open card goes back into your own pile.

Winning the game

Two stones home
A stone that reaches the opponent's back row (the goal row) has crossed: it leaves the board and counts as home; an enemy stone standing there is captured. Whoever brings two stones home first wins. You also win if the other side no longer has two stones on the board and at home together.
Move limit
After 120 moves the game ends: more stones home wins, then more stones on the board; otherwise it is a draw.
